analyzed_vuln.description: SkScan::FillPath decides that no clipping blitter is needed solely from conservative_round_to_int(path.getBounds()) and then passes pathContainedInClip=true to sk_fill_path. For the PoV's pathological finite curved path, fixed-point cubic scan conversion drifts/overflows outside those predicted bounds. Because clipping was disabled, walk_simple_edges emits an out-of-canvas span; SkRasterPipelineBlitter forwards its x/y directly to the compiled pipeline, and srcover_rgba_8888 computes an invalid destination pointer and crashes while loading it. The raster-pipeline load is only the crash site; the root cause is the unsafe clipping-elision decision in FillPath.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Fuzzer bytes construct canvas operations culminating in a finite convex/curved path and SrcOver paint on the fixed 128x160 N32 premul raster surface. The path's reported/conservatively rounded bounds are judged contained by the device clip, causing SkScanClipper to omit horizontal clipping, but cubic fixed-point edge walking produces at least one span beyond the surface. That unchecked span flows through walk_simple_edges -> SkRasterPipelineBlitter::blitH/blitRect -> compiled srcover_rgba_8888, where ptr_at_xy uses the invalid coordinates for an out-of-bounds read (and eventual write).

args: Analyze the clipping-elision logic in SkScan::FillPath in skia/src/core/SkScan_Path.cpp, especially pathContainedInClip and SkScanClipper. What minimal root-cause fix would ensure pathological cubic fixed-point edge walking can never emit spans outside the supplied SkRegion clip, while preserving normal behavior? Identify whether always forcing clipping in this entry point is correct, and note any inverse-fill or region-clip semantics.

The provided UBSan crash shows walk_simple_edges emitting an out-of-canvas span through SkRasterPipelineBlitter after SkScan::FillPath judged conservative_round_to_int(path.getBounds()) contained by the clip and passed pathContainedInClip=true to sk_fill_path. A finite pathological curved path has fixed-point cubic scan conversion drift/overflow outside those predicted bounds. The target is skia/src/core/SkScan_Path.cpp and edits must address unsafe clipping elision at its root rather than hardening the unrelated raster pipeline crash site. I am inspecting FillPath, sk_fill_path, and SkScanClipper to determine whether pathContainedInClip should simply never be true for curved paths or whether clipping should always remain active.
